mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering equity discount rates and increasing present value of future cash flows, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines in prior 20 days but S&P 500 returns are negative in >60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in <55% of instances where UNRATE rises >0.2pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer demand, boosting corporate revenues and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise but S&P 500 returns are negative in >45% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During supply shock regimes characterized by declining industrial production, S&P 500 experiences negative returns over 60 trading days due to reduced output and inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline >1.5% YoY but S&P 500 returns positive in >55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth >2% but S&P 500 returns negative in >40% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL rise >0.3pp in 3 months) signals potential Fed tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns positive in >55% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises >0.3pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise but S&P 500 returns positive in >45% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS >4.5%), S&P 500 experiences negative returns over 20 trading days due to higher borrowing costs and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS >4.5% but S&P 500 returns positive in >55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
